info.title: Pizza 4P's POS Store Box API
info.description: What a store's edge calls on its cloud: the store-facing `/sync` surface, and `/activate` and `/claim`, the two ways a box first comes to hold a credential. Generated from the handlers (ADR-0177). Every failure carries the AIP-193 `ErrorResponse` envelope, and the whole surface is rate-limited per client before any credential is read.

post.summary:
A device exchanges its activation code for a credential (unauthenticated — the code is the
credential). Single-use and deny-by-default, per [`pos_core::activation::redeem`].

requestBody.description: `code`, the activation code from the store's setup sheet, and optionally the `store_id` the box expects to belong to

201.description: Activated: the `device_id`, and the device `credential`, returned this once; the cloud keeps only its hash (ADR-0050)

400.description: The code or the store id is malformed

403.description: Refused: a spent, revoked, unknown or raced code, or one issued for another store, all answer the same

429.description: Too many activation attempts from this client: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The activation service, or the OS entropy source, is unavailable

post.x-public-reason: a single-use activation code from the store's setup sheet

post.summary: A box opens a claim. Unauthenticated: the box has nothing to authenticate with yet.

201.description: A claim: its `claim_id`, the `user_code` the box shows, the `secret` it keeps to collect with, when it expires, and how often to poll (ADR-0148)

429.description: Too many activation attempts from this client: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The claim store, or the OS entropy source, is unavailable

post.x-public-reason: nothing: its code works only once the console binds it

post.summary:
A box polls for its credential. `202` while nobody has bound the code, the credential once it
has, `409` with reason `EXPIRED` when the hour is over, and one `403` for everything else.

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: The claim the box opened, a ULID

requestBody.description: `secret`, the one the claim was opened with

200.description: Bound: the box's `tenant_id`, `store_id` and `device_id`, and its device `credential`, returned this once

202.description: Nobody has bound the code yet: `status` is `PENDING`, and the box asks again

403.description: This claim cannot be collected. Every such refusal answers the same, so it reveals nothing

409.description: The claim has expired (`EXPIRED`): open a new one

429.description: Too many collection polls from this client: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The claim store, or the OS entropy source, is unavailable

post.x-public-reason: the secret the claim was opened with

post.summary: `POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/archive?taken_at=` — a store ships a sealed archive.
post.description:
The cloud is a **sink for bytes it cannot read**. It does not open the archive, does not parse
it, and holds no key material for it beyond the wrapped column — the seal happened at the till
precisely so that a store's buyer details ([ADR-0107](../../../docs/adr/0107-the-buyer-is-a-subject.md))
never exist here in plaintext.

What it *does* check is the header: eight magic bytes and a format version, so an obviously
wrong body (a plain database, a truncated download, an HTML error page from a proxy) is refused
at upload instead of discovered at restore. That is a shape check and emphatically not
verification — only the key opens an archive, and the cloud has none.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

parameters.name: taken_at
parameters.description: When the store took the archive, in milliseconds since the epoch by its own clock

requestBody.description: The sealed archive's bytes, as `pos-edge archive` writes them. The cloud checks the header and cannot open the rest

200.description: Stored: the archive's `object_key`, `size_bytes` and `sha256`, for the store to log

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, taken_at is not a positive time, or the body is not a store archive

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

413.description: The body is larger than 256 MiB

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

500.description: The archive's storage key could not be built

503.description: The credential store, or the object store or archive registry, is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/archive-key` — the key this store seals its archives with, minted
on the first ask.
post.description:
Mint-on-first-ask rather than an admin action, because a store that starts archiving must not
need somebody to have remembered; the console reveals and rotates it afterwards. The mint is
insert-if-absent in one statement ([`ArchiveStore::adopt_key`]), so two tills asking in the same
second get the *same* key rather than two — one of which would be the key to archives nobody
could open.

A `POST` for a value that reads like a `GET`, and deliberately so: the first call has a side
effect that outlives it. A `GET` that mints is one a caching proxy or a browser prefetch may
perform unasked, and the thing it would create here is the key to every archive this store ever
ships.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

200.description: `key`: the key this store seals its archives with, minted on the first ask (ADR-0124)

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

500.description: The stored key cannot be opened with the configured secret, or no key could be minted

503.description: The credential store, or the archive registry, is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/artifact` — hands a store the signed release bytes it decided to
install ([ADR-0088](../../../docs/adr/0088-ota-artifact-hosting.md)).
post.description:
**The cloud is a dumb host.** It stores bytes an operator uploaded and hands them back; it never
signs, and it never verifies the minisign signature. The edge verifies against a trust anchor
baked into its own binary ([ADR-0047](../../../docs/adr/0047-minisign-verification.md),
[ADR-0092](../../../docs/adr/0092-artifact-trust-chain.md)), so a compromised cloud, a swapped
blob or a spoofed host can make an update *fail* — never make a box install code.

**`read_config`, the owner's call (2026-09-04).** Every provisioned box already carries that
scope, so the OTA path works with no re-provisioning; a dedicated `fetch_update` scope would be
cleaner and would cost a visit to every live store before a single update could ship. The scope
is here to stop the VPS being an open binary-distribution host, not to keep a signed artifact
secret.

The signature rides `X-Pos-Artifact-Signature` as lowercase hex and the body stays the raw
artifact: a JSON envelope would mean encoding tens of megabytes to carry a few hundred bytes. The
blob holds **raw** signature bytes — ADR-0092 Correction 2 put minisign's base64 decode at the
`/admin` upload, once, under operator supervision, so the edge never sees base64 for a signature.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `release`, the release tag, and `arch`, the target the store runs

200.description: The release's binary as `application/octet-stream`, its detached signature in the `X-Pos-Artifact-Signature` header as lowercase hex (ADR-0092). The edge verifies both before it installs anything

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or release or arch is not well formed

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

404.description: The cloud hosts no artifact for that release on that target

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

500.description: The release is recorded but its binary or signature is missing, the stored binary does not match its recorded digest, or the signature could not be sent

503.description: The credential store, or the release registry or artifact store, is unavailable

get.summary:
Serves a store its own configuration update: nothing (up to date), a delta, or a full snapshot
past *K* versions behind ([ADR-0039](../../../docs/adr/0039-config-delivery.md)).
get.description:
Requires a valid API key with the `read_config` scope, and answers **only** for that key's tenant:
the tenant comes from the verified grant, never the path, so a store can pull a `store_id` only
within its own tenant. A store outside the tenant, or one with nothing published, reads `404`.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

parameters.name: held_version
parameters.description: The config version the store holds, a ULID. Absent when it holds none

200.description: `status`: `up_to_date`, or `update` with the snapshot or collapsed delta that brings the store to the current version (ADR-0039)

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or held_version is not a ULID

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

404.description: Nothing is published for this store in the credential's tenant

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the configuration service, is unavailable

get.summary:
A store lists its **approved** devices (`manage_devices` scope) — what the edge acts on, never a
raw discovery.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

200.description: The store's approved devices, never a raw discovery

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `manage_devices` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the device service, is unavailable

post.summary:
A store proposes a discovered device (`manage_devices` scope). Stored `pending` for an operator to
approve; the id is minted here and returned once.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: A device the store discovered: `kind` (`printer` or `kds`), `name` and `address` (ADR-0041)

201.description: Proposed: its `id`, and `status` pending until an operator approves it at the console

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, kind is not a known device kind, or name or address is blank

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `manage_devices` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the device service, is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/events` — a store publishes its own events over HTTPS
([ADR-0143](../../../docs/adr/0143-the-device-credential-syncs-and-events-travel-over-https.md)).
post.description:
Scope `publish_events`, which a box's device credential always carries, and the store in the
path must be the credential's. **Every envelope must name that store**: a batch with any other
store in it is refused whole, so no credential can write another shop's history. Ingest is the
same idempotent, all-or-nothing [`Cloud::ingest`] the NATS cursor uses, so a batch published
twice is stored once and the answer is the whole batch either way.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `events`: the store's committed event envelopes, oldest first, at most 256 and 4 MiB, each naming this store (ADR-0143)

200.description: `accepted`: how many envelopes the cloud holds, which is the whole batch. Ingest is idempotent, so a batch published twice is stored once

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, the body is not a batch of events, or it carries more than 256

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `publish_events` scope or belongs to another store, or an envelope names another store; the batch is refused whole

413.description: The body is larger than 4 MiB

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store or the event store is unavailable, and nothing was committed

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/events/hello` — the protocol negotiation for the HTTPS event link
([ADR-0024](../../../docs/adr/0024-protocol-version-negotiation.md), ADR-0143), run on the cloud's side with
the cloud's own window. Answers `200` with the [`HelloOutcome`](pos_proto::protocol::HelloOutcome)
either way: a refusal is an answer, not an error, and the store keeps trading on it.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: The store's protocol `Hello`, naming this store and the protocol versions it speaks (ADR-0024)

200.description: The negotiation's outcome, an agreed version or a refusal. A refusal is an answer, not an error, and the store keeps trading on it

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or the body is not a hello

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `publish_events` scope or belongs to another store, or the hello names another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

post.summary:
`POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/heartbeat` — a store's lightweight liveness ping
([ADR-0068](../../../docs/adr/0068-fleet-liveness.md) slice 2). Authenticated with the same scoped
API key the config pull uses (`read_config`), it advances the store's `last_seen_at` and nothing
else, so a store that is up but not currently pulling config (a parked long-poll, a quiet period
between publishes) still registers as online. `204` on success; unlike the config-pull capture,
recording is this request's whole purpose, so a store-write failure is a `503` the edge retries,
not a swallowed best-effort write.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: Optional: `outbox_depth`, `lease_generation` and `print_agents`, each left out when the store cannot say. An empty body is a bare ping

204.description: Recorded: the store's last contact, and what it reported

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or the body is not a heartbeat report

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the configuration service, is unavailable

get.summary: `GET /sync/stores/{store_id}/orders` — the store pulls its pending batch (bounded long-poll).

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

200.description: The store's pending relayed orders, each with its `queued_id` and the `order`. Held open for a bounded wait while there are none, and empty if none arrives

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `relay_orders` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the order queue, is unavailable

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: The store's `outcome`: `accepted`, with the store's order id, its total and its queue number where the channel issues one; or `rejected`, with the refusal's `status` and `message`

204.description: Recorded. A repeated acknowledgement also answers 204

400.description: store_id or queued_id is not a ULID

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `relay_orders` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the order queue, is unavailable

post.summary: `POST /sync/stores/{store_id}/reconcile` — the **store's** door onto the same diff.
post.description:
Identity comes from the scoped key the box presents, not from a body it writes: the tenant is the
grant's and the store is the path's, checked against the key's binding. That is the same shape the
config pull, the heartbeat and the OTA report have, and it is why this route needs no shared
secret — a store cannot reach the cloud's private network, and never could
(production-readiness **R3**).

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `event_ids`: the ids of events the store holds, each a ULID

200.description: `missing`: the ids the cloud does not hold, for the store to publish again

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or an event id is not a ULID

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the reconciliation store, is unavailable

post.summary:
Records one store's OTA report ([ADR-0078](../../../docs/adr/0078-sync-and-ota-closure.md)).
Internal (the reporting partner of `/internal/ingest`), so it is absent from the public OpenAPI
and requires the `X-Pos-Internal-Key` shared secret
([ADR-0097](../../../docs/adr/0097-internal-route-authentication.md)) on top of the proxy denies.
A malformed id or an empty version is a `400`; a store failure is a retryable `503`; success is
`204`. The key does not make the report *attributable* — the store id rides in the body — which is
A **store** reports the version it is running, on the route that can say who it is.
post.description:
The tenant comes from the scoped key and the store from the path, so a report is
tenant-attributable — which the `/internal` shape could not be at any strength of secret, because
it read both out of the body ([ADR-0097](../../../docs/adr/0097-internal-route-authentication.md)).

**What this does not close.** A [`Grant`](crate::auth::apikey::Grant) pins a tenant, not a store,
so a key issued to one store can still name a sibling store of the *same tenant* in the path.
That is a real residual and it is stated rather than glossed: the move closes cross-tenant
forgery, not intra-tenant. It is bounded by what a report *is* — pure telemetry that never changes
what any box runs (ADR-0078) — so the worst outcome is a distorted rollout picture for one
operator's own fleet. Closing it needs a store-scoped grant, which is a key-issuance change and
its own slice.

Gated on `read_config`, for the reason [`serve_ota_artifact`] is: every provisioned box already
carries it, so the OTA path works with no re-provisioning, and a report is not a secret.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: The store, a ULID. It must be the credential's own

requestBody.description: `installed`, the release the store now runs, and `self_test_passed` where it has run its post-install self-test (ADR-0078)

400.description: store_id is not a ULID, or installed is blank

401.description: No credential, or one the cloud does not accept: one answer for every credential problem

403.description: The credential lacks the `read_config` scope, or belongs to another store

429.description: Too many requests to the store sync surface: `Retry-After` says when to try again

503.description: The credential store, or the fleet store, is unavailable

ErrorBody.description: The error body — the schema mirror of [`pos_proto::error::ErrorBody`].

code.description: The HTTP status code, repeated here so a body is self-describing once logged.

details.description: Field-level detail. Absent when the failure is not about a particular field.

message.description: A human-readable explanation. Never contains personal data, because responses are logged.

ErrorDetail.description:
One reason a request failed, tied to the field responsible — the schema mirror of
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorDetail`].

field.description:
The offending field, in the same `snake_case` name the request used. For a whole-request
fault this can be a header name (`if-match`) rather than a body field.

reason.description:
A stable, machine-readable reason such as `MUST_BE_POSITIVE` or `INVALID_ENUM_VALUE`. Stable
so a client can branch on it; `message` is for people and may be reworded at any time.

ErrorResponse.description:
The envelope every `/admin` failure carries — the schema mirror of
[`pos_proto::error::ErrorResponse`].

One level of nesting so a response is unambiguous at the top level: a success body is the record,
a failure body is `{"error": …}`.

device_credential.description: A box's device credential, issued once by `/activate` or a collected claim, or its store's scoped API key, presented as a bearer token. Each requirement's role is the scope the route checks, and the credential answers only for its own store.

tags.name: configuration
tags.description: The store's published configuration, pulled as a snapshot or a delta, and its liveness heartbeat (ADR-0039, ADR-0068).

tags.name: events
tags.description: The store's own events, published over HTTPS after a protocol hello, and the reconciliation that finds what the cloud is missing (ADR-0143, ADR-0024, ADR-0078).

tags.name: order relay
tags.description: Orders taken for the store elsewhere, pulled by a bounded long-poll and acknowledged with the store's outcome (ADR-0061).

tags.name: updates
tags.description: The signed release a store installs, and what it reports once it runs it (ADR-0088, ADR-0078).

tags.name: archives
tags.description: The key a store seals its archives with, and the sealed archives it ships, which the cloud cannot open (ADR-0124).

tags.name: devices
tags.description: Printers and kitchen displays a store discovers and proposes, and the ones an operator approved (ADR-0041).

tags.name: box activation
tags.description: How a box first comes to hold its device credential: an activation code from the setup sheet, or a claim the console binds (ADR-0050, ADR-0148).
